The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14223512/assets/a71217d2b2e610b38f78f4471cc122de7098708900e3658cda449118df0e63dd.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes of the slope field are horizontal along the lines $x=0$ and $y=-1,$ as shown above. Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on both of these lines.

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}={x}^{2}(y+1)^{2} \\ {y}^{′} & =x(y+1)\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the lines $x=0$ and $y=-1$ divide the plane into $4$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $4$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| $y>-1$ | $↗$

$(+)$ | $↗$

$(+)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | $↗$

$(+)$ | $↗$

$(+)$ |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |

 
Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}={x}^{2}(y+1)^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}={x}^{2}{y}^{2}+2{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}.$
